nodes.description: FSHB encodes the beta subunit that gives FSH its receptor specificity. Reported alleles are a two-nucleotide frameshift deletion (historically Val61X), a one-nucleotide frameshift (c.289delG), nonsense variants (Tyr76X, Arg97X, p.Arg115Ter, p.Cys122Ter) and missense substitutions of conserved cystine-knot cysteines (Cys51Gly, Cys82Arg). Truncations remove the regions needed for association with the alpha subunit and for receptor binding; the cysteine substitutions prevent formation of disulphide bonds needed for correct folding.

nodes.description: Exogenous FSH replaces the missing hormone at its intact receptor. In women, recombinant or urinary FSH induces follicle growth, estradiol and inhibin B production and ovulation; the first reported woman conceived. Because LH is already high, the ovarian response can be excessive, and multifollicular development with signs of hyperstimulation has been reported, so dosing needs close monitoring. In a treated man testicular volume increased and spermatocytes appeared in semen after a year, without a reported pregnancy.
